q.s: The Harappan site of Dholavira in the Rann of Kutch is known locally by which name?
q.x: Dholavira on Khadir island in Kutch is locally called Kotada; Kot Bala is Balakot in Baluchistan.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Gujarat?
q.x: Kalibangan ('black bangles') is in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan; the other three are in Gujarat.

q.s: Dholavira, one of the five largest Harappan cities, was built mainly of which material, unlike most Harappan sites?
q.x: Dholavira used dressed sandstone and limestone blocks, whereas most Harappan cities used baked bricks.

q.s: The Harappan dockyard at Lothal was connected with which water body?
q.x: Lothal's dock was joined to the Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay) through a channel.

q.s: Which of the following was the westernmost port of the Harappan civilisation?
q.x: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast of Baluchistan was the westernmost Harappan site and port.

q.s: In the Sindhi language, the name of the Harappan city Mohenjodaro means:
q.x: Mohenjodaro means 'Mound of the Dead' in Sindhi; Lothal means the same in Gujarati.

q.s: The Harappans were the first to grow cotton, which the Greeks called by which name?
q.x: The Greeks called cotton Sindon (from Sind); Meluhha was the Mesopotamian name for the Indus region.

q.s: Which of the following crops was NOT grown by the Harappans?
q.x: Maize is an American crop introduced much later; wheat, barley, sesame and mustard were Harappan crops.

q.s: Evidence of salt production in the Harappan period has been found at which site in Gujarat?
q.x: Kerala-no-dhoro (Padri) has yielded evidence of salt making; Kuntasi had bead and copper workshops.

q.s: The Harappans used faience, the world's first glazed ware, for all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Faience (glazed ground silica) was used for beads, bangles, amulets and small figurines, not big storage jars.

q.s: In the Rigvedic period, the term 'Karmara' referred to which craftsman?
q.x: Karmara was the smith; the potter was Kulala and the goldsmith Hiranyakara.

q.s: In the Rigvedic economy, the craftsman called 'Takshan' was a:
q.x: Takshan was the carpenter (chariot maker); Kulala was the potter and Vaya the weaver.

q.s: Which of the following Rigvedic terms does NOT denote a craftsman?
q.x: Gavishti means 'search for cows', i.e. war; Kulala, Vaya and Hiranyakara were potter, weaver and goldsmith.

q.s: Which of the following statements about guilds (shrenis) of ancient India is correct?
o: They were forbidden to fix prices and wages.
They framed their own rules called shreni-dharma.
They first appeared only in the Gupta period.
Their head was always appointed by the king.
q.x: Guilds had their own shreni-dharma, fixed prices and wages, and had elected or hereditary heads (jetthaka/pamukha).

q.s: Rajghat, which has yielded punch-marked coins and seals with Greek inscriptions, is a site near:
q.x: Rajghat lies in Varanasi and is a key site of the Second Urbanisation in the Ganga valley.

q.s: In Buddhism, Right View and Right Intention of the Eightfold Path together form:
q.x: Right View and Right Intention form Prajna (wisdom); speech, action and livelihood form Sila.

q.s: Which of the following elements of the Eightfold Path does NOT belong to Sila (ethical conduct)?
q.x: Right Mindfulness belongs to Samadhi along with Right Effort and Right Concentration.

q.s: The Buddha performed the 'Twin Miracle' at which place?
q.x: The Twin Miracle took place at Shravasti, where the Buddha also gave most of his sermons.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four great places of Buddhist pilgrimage linked to the Buddha's birth, enlightenment, first sermon and death?
q.x: The four are Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar; Shravasti is linked with the Twin Miracle.

q.s: Which of the following rock-cut caves belong to the Mauryan period?
q.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar date to the Mauryan age (3rd century BCE); Karla is Satavahana period.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built under the patronage of which dynasty?
q.x: The Kailasa temple was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE.

q.s: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
q.x: Simuka (Srimukha) founded the Satavahana line after the Mauryas in the Deccan.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Satavahanas is correct?
o: They succeeded the Guptas in the Deccan.
They had earlier been feudatories of the Mauryas.
q.x: The Satavahanas, once Mauryan feudatories, rose after the Mauryas; the Puranas call them Andhra-bhrityas.

q.s: The Allahabad Pillar Prasasti of Samudragupta was composed by:
q.x: Harisena, Samudragupta's Sandhivigrahika, composed the prasasti; Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Allahabad Prasasti is correct?
o: It is in classical Sanskrit in the champu style, mixing prose and verse.
It is written in the Kharosthi script.
Its composer also wrote the Brihatkatha Kosha.
It is a Prakrit inscription of the Satavahanas.
q.x: It is in Sanskrit champu style in Gupta Brahmi; the Brihatkatha Kosha is by a later Jain Harisena.

q.s: The poet Mayura, author of the Suryashataka, adorned the court of:
q.x: Mayura, like Banabhatta, was a court poet of Harshavardhana.

q.s: Bhavabhuti, author of Uttararamacharita, was patronised by:
q.x: Bhavabhuti wrote Malatimadhava and Uttararamacharita under Yashovarman of Kannauj.

q.s: Who was the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi?
q.x: After Vijayaditya VII died in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with the Chola state.

q.s: Who merged the Vengi kingdom with the Chola state, uniting the Tamil and Andhra regions?
q.x: Kulottunga I, of Chalukya-Chola descent, merged Vengi with the Chola state after 1075.

q.s: Which was the first southern kingdom attacked by Malik Kafur during his Deccan campaigns?
q.x: Kafur attacked Devagiri in 1307-08, then Warangal (1309-10), Dwarasamudra (1310-11) and Madurai (1311).

q.s: Which of the following kingdoms was NOT invaded by Malik Kafur?
q.x: Vijayanagara was founded only in 1336; Kafur attacked the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.

q.s: In the First Battle of Panipat (1526), Babur's flanking tactic was known as:
q.x: Tulughma was the flanking attack; araba was the line of carts chained together as a defence.

q.s: Who commanded Babur's artillery at the First Battle of Panipat?
q.x: Ustad Ali Quli, with Mustafa, was in charge of Babur's guns at Panipat.

q.s: Sultan Garhi, regarded as the first Islamic tomb in India, was built by:
q.x: Iltutmish built Sultan Garhi (1231) for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud.

q.s: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Delhi was built by:
q.x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Purana Qila was built by Sher Shah Suri in 1541.

q.s: Amir Khusrau, who called himself 'Tuti-i-Hind', is regarded as the father of which language form?
q.x: Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli; his Hindavi verses grew into Rekhta/Urdu.

q.s: Which poet of the Delhi Sultanate was called 'Sadi-i-Hind' for his ghazals?
q.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi was called the Sadi of India; Khusrau was the Parrot of India.

q.s: Akbar's conquest of Gondwana in 1564 was opposed by which ruler?
q.x: Rani Durgavati of Gondwana resisted Asaf Khan's army in 1564; Baz Bahadur ruled Malwa.

q.s: Which of the following rulers did NOT oppose Akbar's conquests of the 1560s?
q.x: Rana Sanga fought Babur at Khanwa (1527); Baz Bahadur, Udai Singh and Surjan Rai lost Malwa, Chittor and Ranthambore to Akbar.

q.s: Which of the following events did NOT take place in the reign of Jahangir?
q.x: Samugarh (1658) was fought in Shah Jahan's war of succession; Kandahar was lost in 1622, Kangra taken in 1620 and Mewar submitted in 1615.

q.s: By the Treaty of 1615 with Jahangir, which Mewar ruler submitted to the Mughals?
q.x: Rana Amar Singh submitted in 1615 and his son Karan Singh was made a Mughal mansabdar.

q.s: Which Mughal general seized Emperor Jahangir on the banks of the Jhelum in 1626?
q.x: Mahabat Khan's coup of 1626 took Jahangir captive on the Jhelum.

q.s: Which of the following statements about revolts in Jahangir's reign is correct?
o: Nur Jahan supported Khurram against Shahryar.
Prince Khurram rebelled in 1606 and was blinded.
Prince Khusrau rebelled in 1606 and was defeated near Lahore.
Mahabat Khan seized Jahangir at Agra in 1622.
q.x: Khusrau rebelled in 1606; Khurram revolted in 1622-26 while Nur Jahan backed Shahryar.

q.s: The share of Hindu nobles in the Mughal nobility rose to about 31.6 per cent under which emperor?
q.x: Athar Ali's study shows Hindu nobles at about 31.6% in 1679-1707, many being Marathas from the Deccan wars.

q.s: Which Mughal official supervised the royal household and the imperial karkhanas?
q.x: The Mir Saman (Khan-i-Saman) managed the household and karkhanas; the Mir Bakhshi headed the military department.

q.s: In the Mughal administration, religious grants such as madad-i-maash were looked after by the:
q.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur handled religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief justice.

q.s: Who among the following was the only woman saint among the twelve Alvars?
q.x: Andal was the only woman among the Alvars; Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Nayanar (Shaiva) saint.

q.s: The Periya Puranam, the hagiography of the Nayanars, was written by Sekkizhar under which Chola king?
q.x: Sekkizhar composed the Periya Puranam in the court of Kulottunga II.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, a Mughal-era Sufi of the 16th-17th century, belonged to which order?
q.x: Sirhindi (1564-1624) was a leading Naqshbandi Sufi, who lived long after Kabir.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Bhakti saint and occupation is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kabir was a weaver; Dhanna was the Jat cultivator.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the successors of Shivaji is correct?
o: Sambhaji was captured at Raigarh and executed in 1700.
Tarabai appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa.
Rajaram directed Maratha resistance from Gingee.
q.x: Rajaram held out at Gingee; Sambhaji was seized at Sangameshwar (1689) and Shahu ruled from Satara.

q.s: Which Maratha ruler appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1713?
q.x: Shahu, ruling from Satara, made Balaji Vishwanath Peshwa in 1713.

q.s: The 'Golden Farman' of 1632 granting the English free trade in its ports was issued by the Sultan of:
q.x: The Sultan of Golconda issued the Golden Farman (1632) for an annual payment of 500 pagodas.

q.s: Bombay, received by Charles II as dowry, was given to the East India Company in 1668 for an annual rent of:
q.x: Charles II leased Bombay to the Company in 1668 for 10 pounds a year.

q.s: From whom did the French general Bussy obtain the Northern Circars in 1753?
q.x: Salabat Jang gave the Circars to Bussy to pay for French troops; Muzaffar Jang had died in 1751.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Northern Circars?
q.x: The Circars included Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore, Mustafanagar (Kondapalli) and Guntur; Nellore was not one.

q.s: The city of Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad in 1591 and built the Charminar.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Marco Polo visited Machilipatnam during Qutb Shahi rule.
Machilipatnam attracted Europeans for its chintz and diamonds.
Hyderabad was founded by the Kakatiyas.
Motupalli was the capital of the Qutb Shahis.
q.x: Machilipatnam was famed for chintz and diamonds; Marco Polo had visited Motupalli in the Kakatiya period.

q.s: Which Act introduced the system of 'dual control' over the East India Company's Indian affairs?
q.x: Pitt's India Act created the Board of Control alongside the Court of Directors: dual control.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Charter Act, 1833?
o: End of the Company's commercial functions
Designation of the Governor-General of India
Addition of a Law Member to the Governor-General's Council
q.x: Dual control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784; the 1833 Act made Bentinck Governor-General of India and ended Company trade.

q.s: The end of French power in India came with the British victory in the:
q.x: The Third Carnatic War, decided at Wandiwash (1760), ended French power; the Treaty of Paris (1763) concluded it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Carnatic Wars is correct?
o: At Aix-la-Chapelle Pondicherry was returned to the French.
The Third Carnatic War was an extension of the Seven Years' War.
The First Carnatic War was linked to the War of the Spanish Succession.
The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Second Carnatic War.
q.x: The Third war was part of the Seven Years' War; the First was tied to the Austrian Succession and at Aix-la-Chapelle Madras went back to the English.

q.s: The First Carnatic War between the English and the French was an extension of the:
q.x: The First Carnatic War (1746-48) was linked to the Austrian War of Succession and ended by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle.

q.s: After the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799), which Wodeyar ruler was restored to the throne of Mysore?
q.x: The boy ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was restored under a subsidiary alliance.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799)?
o: The Marathas fought actively and took their share of Mysore.
The Nizam fought as a subsidiary ally of the British.
Arthur Wellesley took part in the campaign.
q.x: The Marathas gave no active help and refused their share; the Nizam got Gooty and Gurramkonda.

q.s: Which of the following districts was NOT part of the 'Ceded Districts' of 1800?
q.x: The Ceded Districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, given by the Nizam in 1800.

q.s: The Ceded Districts came to the East India Company in 1800 from:
q.x: The Nizam ceded his share of Mysore territories to pay for the subsidiary force in 1800.

q.s: The Northern Circar of Chicacole corresponds broadly to which present-day district?
q.x: Chicacole is Srikakulam; Mustafanagar (Kondapalli) corresponds to Krishna.

q.s: The College of Fort William at Calcutta was founded in 1800 by which Governor-General?
q.x: Wellesley (1798-1805) founded Fort William College to train Company civil servants.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Lord Wellesley?
q.x: The Permanent Settlement (1793) was introduced by Cornwallis.

q.s: The Chanda Railway agitation of 1883 in Hyderabad State was led by:
q.x: Dr Aghorenath Chattopadhyaya, father of Sarojini Naidu, led the agitation against the Chanda Railway scheme.

q.s: The Wadi–Secunderabad railway line of the Nizam's State was opened in:
q.x: The Wadi–Secunderabad line opened in October 1874.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta set up in 1774?
q.x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta under the Regulating Act.

q.s: The Federal Court of India was provided for by the:
q.x: The 1935 Act provided for the Federal Court, set up at Delhi in 1937.

q.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: It made the Governor answerable to the provincial legislature.
It introduced dyarchy in the provinces for the first time.
It abolished dyarchy in the provinces.
Its federal dyarchy at the Centre came into operation in 1937.
q.x: The 1935 Act replaced provincial dyarchy with provincial autonomy; the federal part never came into force.

q.s: The Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry was founded in 1878 by:
q.x: Veeresalingam founded the Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry (1878); Venkataratnam Naidu led the Brahmo movement.

q.s: Dr B.R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at:
q.x: Ambedkar was born at Mhow (now Dr Ambedkar Nagar) in Madhya Pradesh, in a Mahar family from Ratnagiri.

q.s: From which institution in London was Dr B.R. Ambedkar called to the bar?
q.x: Ambedkar became a barrister from Gray's Inn; his MSc and DSc were from the London School of Economics.

q.s: The Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar, representing the orthodox wing of the Arya Samaj, was founded by:
q.x: Munshi Ram founded Gurukul Kangri (1902); Lajpat Rai and Hansraj belonged to the DAV (College) party.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Arya Samaj?
q.x: The Atmiya Sabha (1815) was founded by Raja Rammohan Roy; the others belong to the Arya Samaj.

q.s: The Namdhari (Kuka) movement in Punjab was founded by:
q.x: Baba Ram Singh founded the Namdhari sect at Bhaini, Ludhiana, in 1857; the Kukas boycotted British goods and courts.

q.s: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session at Bombay in 1885; Hume founded the Indian National Union.

q.s: Which of the following statements about A.O. Hume is correct?
o: He was promoted by Lord Lytton in 1879.
He founded the Indian Association of Calcutta.
He retired from the ICS in 1882 and settled at Shimla.
He was the first President of the Indian National Congress.
q.x: Hume retired in 1882 after being demoted in 1879 over a clash with Lytton; the Indian Association was Surendranath Banerjee's.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the early (Moderate) Indian National Congress?
o: Separation of the executive from the judiciary
Simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England
q.x: The Moderates sought reforms within British rule; Purna Swaraj was adopted only at Lahore in 1929.

q.s: 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which set out the drain theory, was written by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote the book (1901); R.C. Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.

q.s: The economic nationalist R.C. Dutt presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: R.C. Dutt was President of the 1899 Lucknow session.

q.s: The August Declaration of 1917, promising progressive realisation of responsible government, was made by:
q.x: Secretary of State Edwin Montagu made the declaration on 20 August 1917 in the House of Commons.

q.s: Along with Annie Besant, who among the following was interned in June 1917?
q.x: Besant was interned with B.P. Wadia and George Arundale and released in September 1917.

q.s: Jatin Das died in 1929 in Lahore jail after a hunger strike lasting:
q.x: Jatin Das fasted 63 days for political-prisoner status and died on 13 September 1929.

q.s: Mahatma Gandhi attended which Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Congress?
q.x: Gandhi attended only the Second Conference (1931), after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Congress boycotted the other two.

q.s: Gandhi's Phoenix Settlement in South Africa (1904) was located near:
q.x: Phoenix Settlement was near Durban; Tolstoy Farm (1910) was near Johannesburg.

q.s: The Tripuri session of the Congress (1939), where Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected President, was held near:
q.x: Tripuri is near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh; Bose had first presided at Haripura (1938).

q.s: Who chaired the National Planning Committee set up by the Congress in 1938?
q.x: Under Bose's presidency, the Congress set up the National Planning Committee with Nehru as chairman.

q.s: B.C. Dutt is remembered for his role in which event of 1946?
o: INA trials at the Red Fort
q.x: B.C. Dutt, a rating of HMIS Talwar, was a central figure in the RIN revolt of February 1946.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 is correct?
o: Referendums were to be held in Punjab and Bengal.
The Boundary Commissions were to be headed by Lord Mountbatten.
Sindh was to decide its future through its own Assembly.
Partition needed a two-thirds majority of the whole Punjab Assembly.
q.x: Sindh's Assembly decided; referendums were held in NWFP and Sylhet, and a simple majority of either group in Punjab or Bengal meant partition.

q.s: Who headed the Boundary Commissions set up for the partition of Punjab and Bengal in 1947?
q.x: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both Boundary Commissions.

q.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, leader of the Chirala-Perala movement, was popularly known as:
q.x: Duggirala was 'Andhra Ratna'; Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari' and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao 'Desoddharaka'.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State formed in 1953?
q.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State with Kurnool as capital.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast for a separate Andhra State that lasted:
q.x: His 58-day fast led to Nehru's announcement of Andhra State.

q.s: The Razakars, the militant volunteer force of the Majlis-e-Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen in Hyderabad, were led by:
q.x: Qasim Razvi led the Razakars; Mir Laik Ali was the Nizam's last prime minister.

q.s: The 'Tribal Panchsheel', the principles of Nehru's tribal policy, is credited to:
q.x: The Tribal Panchsheel, favouring integration with respect for tribal identity, is credited to Verrier Elwin.

q.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, PESA, was enacted in:
q.x: PESA, 1996 extends Part IX to the Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam's ministry in Andhra State fell in November 1954 over which issue?
q.x: Prakasam's ministry was defeated on 15 November 1954 over prohibition, leading to President's rule.

q.s: Which party was NOT part of the United Congress that won the 1955 mid-term poll in Andhra State?
q.x: The United Congress of Congress, Krishikar Lok Party and PSP won 119 seats against the Communists.

q.s: The 'Ramadandu' volunteer corps was organised in the Chirala-Perala movement of 1921 by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organised the Ramadandu during the Chirala-Perala movement.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam served early in his career as municipal chairman of which town?
q.x: Prakasam was municipal chairman of Rajahmundry.

q.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during the Jai Andhra movement of 1972?
q.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM; President's Rule followed on 18 January 1973.

q.s: Daimabad, which yielded a bronze chariot and buffalo, is located on the banks of which river?
q.x: Daimabad, the largest Jorwe site and the southernmost Late Harappan site, lies on the Pravara in Ahmednagar.

q.s: A minor rock edict of Ashoka has been found in Andhra Pradesh at:
q.x: Rajula Mandagiri (Kurnool) has a minor rock edict; Amaravati yielded a pillar-edict fragment.

q.s: Which of the following sites in Andhra Pradesh has NOT yielded an Ashokan edict?
q.x: Erragudi has major and minor rock edicts, Rajula Mandagiri a minor rock edict and Amaravati a pillar fragment.

q.s: The Indian National Calendar based on the Saka era was adopted on 22 March 1957. Its first month is:
q.x: The national calendar begins with Chaitra; 1 Chaitra falls on 22 March (21 March in a leap year).

q.s: The Saka era, used in the Indian National Calendar, began in:
q.x: The Saka era begins in 78 CE; 57 BCE is the Vikrama era and 320 CE the Gupta era.

q.s: The Satavahana king Hala, known as 'Kavivatsala', compiled which Prakrit work?
q.x: Hala compiled the Gathasaptasati; Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha.

q.s: Who first identified the Amaravati stupa site in 1797?
q.x: Colin Mackenzie identified Amaravati in 1797; Sewell excavated it in 1877.

q.s: On the ayakapatas of Amaravati, the Buddha's birth is depicted by the symbol of the:
q.x: Lotus = birth, horse = renunciation, Bodhi tree = enlightenment, wheel = first sermon, stupa = parinirvana.

q.s: In Amaravati art, which of the following pairs of symbol and event is NOT correct?
q.x: The Bodhi tree stands for enlightenment; the lotus stands for birth.

q.s: Nagarjunakonda was the main centre of which school of art in its final, mature phase?
q.x: Ikshvaku carving at Nagarjunakonda is the last phase of the Amaravati school, with Buddha's life and Jatakas as themes.

q.s: The Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi was founded by:
q.x: Pulakeshin II conquered Vengi and made his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana its ruler.

q.s: The Addanki inscription of Pandaranga, the first Telugu verse inscription, is composed in which metre?
q.x: Pandaranga, general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, left the Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre.

q.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was made viceroy of Vengi by Pulakeshin II in about:
q.x: Pulakeshin II took Vengi from the Vishnukundins c. 616 and installed Kubja Vishnuvardhana in 617.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Telugu language is correct?
o: It belongs to the South-Central branch of the Dravidian family.
It belongs to the Indo-Aryan family.
It shares its branch with Malayalam and Tulu.
Niccolo de' Conti called it the 'Sanskrit of the South'.
q.x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian with Gondi and Kui; Niccolo de' Conti called it the 'Italian of the East'.

q.s: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, champion of spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu, was born on 29 August 1863.

q.s: 'Kavibrahma', one of the Kavitraya of the Telugu Mahabharata, is the title of:
q.x: Tikkana is Kavibrahma; Nannaya is Adikavi and Errana is Prabandha Parameswara.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Palkuriki Somanatha?
q.x: The Andhra Mahabhagavatam is Bammera Potana's; the other three are Somanatha's.

q.s: The Thousand Pillar temple at Hanumakonda was built by the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) built the Thousand Pillar temple in 1163.

q.s: After the Tughlaq conquest of 1323, the Kakatiya capital Orugallu (Warangal) was renamed:
q.x: The Tughlaqs renamed Warangal Sultanpur after 1323.

q.s: The Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of 1163, recording Kakatiya independence, was composed by:
q.x: Achitendru composed the inscription of Rudradeva; Jayapa wrote the Nritta Ratnavali.

q.s: Mahmud Gawan, the famous minister of the Bahmani kingdom, was executed in 1481 by:
q.x: Muhammad Shah III executed Gawan in 1481 on a forged letter; the kingdom broke up soon after.

q.s: Saluva Narasimha shifted his capital from Kalyanapuram to:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha ruled from Chandragiri; Penukonda became the Aravidu capital after Talikota.

q.s: 'Saluvabhyudayam', a work on Saluva Narasimha, was written by his court poet:
q.x: Rajanatha Dindima wrote Saluvabhyudayam; Gangadevi wrote Madhuravijayam.

q.s: Which poet of Krishnadevaraya's court bore the title 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha'?
q.x: Allasani Peddana, author of Manucharitra, was Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

q.s: Which of the following poets was NOT one of the Ashtadiggajas of Krishnadevaraya's court?
q.x: Errana, called Prabandha Parameswara, lived in the 14th century under the Reddis.

q.s: After his Kalinga campaign, Krishnadevaraya married the daughter of which Gajapati ruler?
q.x: Krishnadevaraya married Prataparudra Gajapati's daughter (Tukka/Bhadradevi) and returned lands north of the Krishna.

q.s: After suppressing the Palegars of the Ceded Districts, Thomas Munro introduced which land revenue system there?
q.x: Munro introduced the Ryotwari system in the Ceded Districts, settling revenue directly with the cultivator.

q.s: The Malkapuram inscription of 1261, describing a college and hospital at Mandadam, belongs to the reign of:
q.x: The Malkapuram inscription is of Rudramadevi's reign; it records Visvesvara Sambhu's institutions.

q.s: The Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi was built by Virupanna and Veeranna, officers of which Vijayanagara ruler?
q.x: The Penukonda governors Virupanna and Veeranna built Lepakshi c. 1530-40 under Achyutadevaraya.

q.s: In the Qutb Shahi period, elephants were imported into Andhra ports mainly from:
q.x: Elephants came from Ceylon; Persia and Arabia supplied horses.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Qutb Shahi-era trade of coastal Andhra is correct?
o: Horses were imported mainly from Ceylon.
English purchases of chintz and calico were financed with bullion.
Textiles ranked second only to saltpetre.
q.x: The English paid in bullion; pintado meant printed cloth and textiles ranked second only to diamonds.

q.s: 'Yayati Charitra' (1572), a kavya in pure (achcha) Telugu, was written by:
q.x: Ponnekanti Telaganaryudu's Yayati Charitra avoided Sanskrit words entirely.

q.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's tour of Andhra in 1907 was organised by Mutnuri Krishna Rao, editor of:
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited the Krishna Patrika; Andhra Patrika was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's.

q.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's lectures in Rajahmundry in 1907 are associated with which movement?
q.x: Pal's 1907 tour spread the Vandemataram movement in Andhra after the partition of Bengal.

q.s: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam was founded in 1910 by:
q.x: Kopalle Hanumantha Rao was its founder and first principal and made weaving a subject there.

q.s: Which Andhra leader was given the title 'Desoddharaka'?
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was Desoddharaka; Konda Venkatappayya was Desabhakta.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of leader and popular title is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Andhra Kesari was Prakasam; Konda Venkatappayya was Desabhakta.

q.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Bill was introduced in 1947 by Revenue Minister:
q.x: Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947; the Act got assent in April 1949.

q.s: The 1937 committee that held that the land belongs to the tiller and the zamindar is only a tax collector was headed by:
q.x: The Prakasam Committee of the Madras Legislature reported in November 1938.

q.s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra State formed in 1953?
q.x: C.M. Trivedi, earlier Special Officer for Andhra State, became its first Governor.

q.s: In 2014, the committee for allocation of State government employees between AP and Telangana was headed by:
q.x: The Kamalanathan committee allocated employees; Sheela Bhide dealt with Schedule IX institutions.

q.s: The classic Telugu film 'Pathala Bhairavi' (1951) was directed by:
q.x: Pathala Bhairavi was K.V. Reddy's; K. Viswanath is best known for Sankarabharanam.

q.s: When Pingali Venkayya showed his flag design at the Bezwada AICC session of 1921, Gandhi suggested adding:
q.x: Gandhi asked for the charkha; the Ashoka Chakra replaced it only in 1947.

q.s: Pingali Venkayya, designer of the early tricolour and called 'Jhanda Venkayya', was born at:
q.x: Venkayya was born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru in Krishna district.

q.s: Udayana, the king of Vatsa who married Vasavadatta, had his capital at:
q.x: Vatsa's capital was Kausambi; Vasavadatta was the daughter of Pradyota of Avanti.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the sixteen Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Kalinga does not appear in the Anguttara Nikaya list of sixteen Mahajanapadas.

q.s: The Navabrahma temples of Alampur, called the western gateway of Srisailam, were built by the:
q.x: The nine Navabrahma temples are early Chalukya (Badami) Shiva temples on the Tungabhadra.

q.s: Alampur, known as 'Dakshina Kashi', is situated on the banks of the:
q.x: Alampur stands on the Tungabhadra near its confluence with the Krishna, in Jogulamba Gadwal district.

q.s: The study of jointness of families in the town of Mahuva, Gujarat, was carried out by:
q.x: I.P. Desai's Mahuva study identified degrees of jointness and found nuclear households in the majority.

q.s: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the sapinda relationship extends on the father's side to:
q.x: Sapinda extends five generations through the father and three through the mother.

q.s: The work 'The Hindu Method of Tribal Absorption' (1941) was written by:
q.x: N.K. Bose wrote it; Ghurye described tribes as 'backward Hindus'.

q.s: Which scholar described tribals in India as 'backward Hindus'?
q.x: Ghurye viewed tribes as backward Hindus, opposing Elwin's isolation approach.

q.s: Which of the following statements about tribal society in India is correct?
o: T.K. Oommen proposed the tribe-caste continuum.
Youth dormitories are a feature of caste-based peasant society.
Verrier Elwin described the 'Hindu method of tribal absorption'.
About 90 per cent of Scheduled Tribes live in rural areas.
q.x: About 89.97% of STs are rural; N.K. Bose described tribal absorption and youth dormitories are typical of tribal society.

q.s: The concept of the 'folk-urban continuum' was proposed by:
q.x: Redfield developed the folk-urban continuum from his Yucatan studies; Wirth wrote 'Urbanism as a way of life'.

q.s: The concepts of 'universalisation' and 'parochialisation' were given by:
q.x: McKim Marriott derived them from his study of Kishan Garhi village.

q.s: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 raised paid maternity leave to:
q.x: The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks.

q.s: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 was brought in response to:
q.x: The Disha Bill was named after the Hyderabad victim of November 2019.

q.s: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 proposed completing trial in a rape case within:
q.x: It proposed 7 days of investigation and 14 days of trial, a total of 21 days.

q.s: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, is chaired by:
q.x: NITI Aayog is a non-statutory body with the Prime Minister as chairperson.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a statutory body?
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution; the others were created by Acts of Parliament.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Stand-Up India scheme is correct?
o: It is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.
It funds expansion of existing enterprises.
It gives loans of up to ₹10 lakh only.
Every bank branch must lend to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.
q.x: Stand-Up India (2016, Finance Ministry) gives ₹10 lakh-₹1 crore loans for greenfield enterprises.

q.s: The Code on Social Security, 2020 consolidated how many existing labour laws?
q.x: The Social Security Code merged 9 laws; all four Labour Codes together subsumed 29.

q.s: How many cities were selected under the Smart Cities Mission launched in 2015?
q.x: The Smart Cities Mission covered 100 cities; AMRUT covered 500.

q.s: PM e-Bus Sewa (2023) aims to provide how many electric buses to cities?
q.x: PM e-Bus Sewa provides 10,000 e-buses on a PPP model.

q.s: The first Disha police station in Andhra Pradesh was opened at:
q.x: The Disha app and the first Disha police station were launched at Rajamahendravaram on 8 February 2020.

q.s: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 proposed completing investigation of rape cases within:
q.x: The Bill proposed 7 days for investigation and 14 for trial.

q.s: Who was the first chairman of the National Commission for Minorities after it became a statutory body?
q.x: Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan headed the statutory NCM; Justice M.H. Beg headed the earlier non-statutory commission.

q.s: India's Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) signed in 2022 was with:
q.x: The 2022 CEPA is with the UAE; the ECTA (2022) is with Australia and the CECPA (2021) with Mauritius.

q.s: The WTO agreement that classifies subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable is the:
q.x: The Subsidies and Countervailing Measures Agreement does this; GATS covers trade in services.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an agreement administered by the WTO?
q.x: The Paris Agreement is under the UNFCCC.

q.s: India's ITEC (Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation) programme was launched in:
q.x: ITEC began on 15 September 1964; the Development Partnership Administration came in 2012.

q.s: The Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of India is headquartered at:
q.x: The EXIM Bank, set up on 1 January 1982, is based in Mumbai.

q.s: India shares its longest land border with which neighbouring country?
q.x: The India-Bangladesh border is about 4,096.7 km, the longest; Afghanistan (106 km) is the shortest.

q.s: India shares its shortest land border with:
q.x: The 106 km border with Afghanistan (in PoK) is India's shortest.

q.s: The ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag set up by the Constituent Assembly in 1947 was chaired by:
q.x: Rajendra Prasad chaired it; the 1931 Congress Flag Committee was under Sardar Patel.

q.s: The system of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
q.x: Single citizenship came from Britain; the USA and Switzerland have dual citizenship.

q.s: The 'basic structure' doctrine of the Constitution was laid down in which case?
q.x: Kesavananda Bharati laid down the basic structure; Minerva Mills reaffirmed it.

q.s: The Supreme Court in Rameshwar Prasad (2006) struck down the dissolution of which State Assembly?
q.x: The Court held the 2005 dissolution of the Bihar Assembly unconstitutional.

q.s: The Rule of Law in the Indian Constitution rests primarily on which Article?
q.x: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws, the basis of the Rule of Law.

q.s: Which new law replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) in 2023?
q.x: The BNSS replaced the CrPC; the BNS replaced the IPC and the BSA the Evidence Act.

q.s: Criminal law and criminal procedure fall under which list of the Seventh Schedule?
q.x: Criminal law (entry 1) and criminal procedure (entry 2) are in the Concurrent List.

q.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted by Parliament in the year:
q.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act is of 1961; the Protection of Civil Rights Act is of 1955.

q.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was passed in:
q.x: The PWDVA was passed in 2005 and came into force on 26 October 2006.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution declares the Directive Principles of State Policy non-justiciable?
q.x: Article 37 says the DPSPs shall not be enforceable by any court but are fundamental in governance.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy?
q.x: Constitutional remedies (Article 32) is a Fundamental Right; the others are in Part IV.

q.s: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
q.x: The First Amendment (1951) created the Ninth Schedule to protect land-reform laws.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review?
q.x: I.R. Coelho (2007) held such laws testable against the basic structure, including Articles 14, 19 and 21.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a constitutional amendment is 'law' under Article 13(2)?
q.x: Golaknath held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights; Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh took the opposite view.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Kesavananda Bharati case is correct?
o: It was decided by a five-judge bench.
It held that Parliament can never amend Fundamental Rights.
It was decided by a 7:6 majority on 24 April 1973.
q.x: The 13-judge bench upheld the 24th Amendment but limited Parliament by the basic structure.

q.s: Under the 106th Amendment, reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha is provided by which Article?
q.x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha, 332A the State Assemblies and 334A the commencement and duration.

q.s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, reserving one-third of seats for women in legislatures, got Presidential assent in:
q.x: It received assent on 28 September 2023; it will take effect after the next delimitation.

q.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
q.x: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations.

q.s: Which Amendment made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill?
q.x: The 24th Amendment (1971) made Presidential assent to amendment bills compulsory.

q.s: The phrase 'constitutional morality', used by Dr Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly, was borrowed from:
q.x: Ambedkar used the phrase of the historian George Grote, meaning fidelity to constitutional values.

q.s: The Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of Article 370 in:
q.x: A five-judge bench upheld the abrogation in December 2023.

q.s: Which of the following Union Territories created in 2019 does NOT have a legislature?
q.x: Jammu and Kashmir UT has a legislature; Ladakh was created without one.

q.s: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha, by a two-thirds resolution, enable Parliament to create new All-India Services?
q.x: Article 312 allows a Rajya Sabha resolution for new All-India Services; Article 249 relates to State List subjects.

q.s: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is provided for under:
q.x: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting, presided over by the Speaker.

q.s: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha submits his resignation to the:
q.x: The Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman; he is removed under Article 90(c).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is correct?
o: He nominates the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons.
He is elected by both Houses jointly.
He can be removed by a resolution under Article 90(c).
q.x: Article 94(c) is for the Speaker; the Chairman nominates the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a standing committee of Parliament?
q.x: The Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc committee; the other three are standing financial committees.

q.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President under:
q.x: Article 148 is for the CAG; Article 76 for the Attorney General and 155 for Governors.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT appointed by the President?
q.x: The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha.

q.s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was provided for by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 99th Amendment inserted Articles 124A-124C; the Supreme Court struck it down in 2015.

q.s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was to be chaired by the:
q.x: The CJI was to chair the NJAC; the Law Minister was a member.

q.s: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, BNSS and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force on:
q.x: The three new criminal laws came into force on 1 July 2024.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
o: Appointment of Governors by the Centre
Division of powers in the Seventh Schedule
q.x: Division of powers is a federal feature; the others give the Constitution its unitary bias.

q.s: The subject of preservation and protection of livestock, including cow slaughter, is listed in the:
q.x: It is Entry 15 of the State List.

q.s: During a National Emergency, Parliament can legislate on State List subjects under which Article?
q.x: Article 250 applies during an Emergency; such laws lapse six months after the Emergency ends.

q.s: Under Article 239, the President administers a Union Territory through an:
q.x: Article 239 provides for administration through an Administrator, designated Lieutenant Governor in some UTs.

q.s: Under which Article can the President, with the State's consent, entrust Union executive functions to a State government?
q.x: Article 258(1) needs the State's consent; Article 256 obliges States to comply with Union laws.

q.s: The Governors' Conference in India is presided over by the:
q.x: The President chairs the Governors' Conference; the Prime Minister chairs the Chief Ministers' Conference.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Centre-State cooperation is correct?
o: Inter-State water tribunals are created under Article 263.
The Governors' Conference is chaired by the Prime Minister.
The Chief Ministers' Conference is presided over by the President.
Inter-State water dispute tribunals are statutory bodies.
q.x: Water tribunals are set up under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956; Article 263 is for the Inter-State Council.

q.s: The All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968 were framed under which Act?
q.x: The Central Government framed them under the All India Services Act, 1951.

q.s: The Supreme Court case that called for fixed tenure of officers and Civil Services Boards was:
q.x: T.S.R. Subramanian (2013) asked for fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards; Prakash Singh dealt with police reforms.

q.s: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
q.x: The NCSK works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and has been non-statutory since 2004.

q.s: The Indian Civil Liberties Union, founded in 1936, was set up on the initiative of:
q.x: Nehru and others founded the ICLU in August 1936.

q.s: World Health Day is observed every year on:
q.x: World Health Day is 7 April; Human Rights Day is 10 December.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005 is correct?
o: NGOs substantially financed by government are excluded from 'public authority'.
The right allows taking files out of the office for inspection.
q.x: Section 2(f) defines information widely, including opinions, advices, e-mails, logbooks and samples.

q.s: The Zonal Councils in India were set up under:
q.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the SR Act, 1956; Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council.

q.s: How many Zonal Councils were created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
q.x: There are five Zonal Councils; the North Eastern Council was set up separately in 1971.

q.s: The PAHAL scheme is the Direct Benefit Transfer of subsidy on:
q.x: PAHAL transfers LPG subsidy into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations was appointed in 1969 by the government of:
q.x: The DMK government of Tamil Nadu set it up; the Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) came from Punjab's Akali Dal.

q.s: The first non-Congress government at the Centre, formed in 1977, was headed by:
q.x: The Janata Party government under Morarji Desai took office in 1977.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a constituent of the Janata Party formed in 1977?
q.x: Janata merged Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and the Socialists; CPI(M) only supported it from outside.

q.s: The ban on publishing exit polls during elections is provided under which section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
q.x: Section 126A bars exit polls from the start of the first phase till half an hour after the last phase closes.

q.s: The Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, aimed at building governance capacity of PRIs, is implemented by the:
q.x: RGSA is run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, with 60:40 Centre-State funding.

q.s: The PESA Act, 1996 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee (1995) recommended self-rule through Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas.

q.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the authority to initiate the process of determining forest rights is the:
q.x: The Gram Sabha initiates the process; DLC gives final approval.

q.s: In the Niyamgiri case (2013), Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining by which company?
q.x: The Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas of Odisha rejected Vedanta's mining project.

q.s: Which of the following statements about women's reservation in Panchayats under Article 243D is correct?
o: It applies only to Gram Panchayats.
Not less than one-third of chairperson offices are reserved for women.
One-half of SC/ST seats must go to SC/ST women.
It lapses with the period fixed under Article 334.
q.x: One-third of seats and chairperson posts at all levels are reserved for women, not tied to Article 334.

q.s: The Tribal Sub-Plan strategy was adopted in India during the:
q.x: The TSP, based on the S.C. Dube Committee (1972), was adopted in the Fifth Plan.

q.s: Which approach to tribal policy was associated with Jawaharlal Nehru?
q.x: Nehru favoured integration; early Elwin argued for isolation and Ghurye for assimilation.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Parts IX and IXA of the Constitution is correct?
o: Article 243T provides for reservation of seats in Municipalities.
The minimum age for Panchayat membership is 25 years.
Article 243Z provides for audit under a law made by Parliament.
Article 243E deals with the State Finance Commission.
q.x: 243T covers municipal reservation; 243Z audit is under State law, 243E is duration and the minimum age is 21.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF) is implemented by:
q.x: APCNF has been run by the Rythu Sadhikara Samstha since 2016.

q.s: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor runs between Dadri and:
q.x: The Western DFC links Dadri to JNPT (Mumbai); the Eastern runs from Ludhiana to Sonnagar.

q.s: The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is conducted through which institution?
o: International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
q.x: MoHFW runs NFHS through IIPS Mumbai.

q.s: According to NFHS-6 (2023-24), India's Total Fertility Rate stood at:
q.x: NFHS-6 reported TFR at 2.0, below the replacement level of 2.1.

q.s: India's first 'Justice City' is planned to come up in which city of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Justice City is planned in the capital city Amaravati.

q.s: Which of the following has NOT been a source of funds for the Amaravati capital works?
o: Union support under the AP Reorganisation commitments
q.x: The 96 works are funded by a mix including World Bank-ADB (₹15,000 crore) and HUDCO (₹11,000 crore) loans, not wholly by the Union.

q.s: The Godavari Urban Development Authority (GUDA), formed in 2017, covers which region?
q.x: GUDA covers the Rajamahendravaram-Kakinada region; TUDA covers Tirupati.

q.s: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is implemented at the national level by:
q.x: PMEGP, formed in 2008 by merging PMRY and REGP, is run by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PMEGP is correct?
o: It was formed by merging MGNREGA and SGSY.
Its margin money subsidy varies from 15 to 35 per cent by category and area.
Its subsidy is a flat 25 per cent for all.
Its maximum project cost is ₹20 lakh for manufacturing.
q.x: The limits are ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services; it merged PMRY and REGP.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's Budget 2026-27, which department has the largest outlay?
q.x: School Education has the largest outlay; Health is fourth.

q.s: The national norm for Fair Price Shops under the PDS is about one shop for every:
q.x: The norm is one FPS per about 2,000 persons; AP has one per about 1,376.

q.s: Door delivery of ration through Mobile Dispensing Units in Andhra Pradesh was discontinued in:
q.x: Door delivery through MDUs was discontinued in 2025, and ration is again drawn from Fair Price Shops.

q.s: Low height-for-age in children, an indicator of chronic malnutrition, is called:
q.x: Stunting is low height-for-age; wasting is low weight-for-height and shows acute malnutrition.

q.s: The coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same population is termed:
q.x: The double burden of malnutrition refers to undernutrition and overnutrition together.

q.s: Personal disposable income is obtained by deducting which item from personal income?
q.x: PDI = Personal income minus personal direct taxes; undistributed profits are deducted earlier from national income.

q.s: The expenditure method of measuring national income is also known as the:
q.x: The expenditure method is the outlay method; the income method is the factor income or distributed share method.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT included in national income under the income method?
q.x: The income method sums compensation, rent, interest, profit and mixed income; transfers are not factor incomes.

q.s: Which of the following activities does NOT belong to the tertiary sector?
q.x: Water supply is a secondary (utility) activity; storage, banking and transport are services.

q.s: According to PLFS 2017-18, India's unemployment rate, called a '45-year high', was:
q.x: PLFS 2017-18 reported 6.1%; PLFS 2025 put it at 3.1%.

q.s: The National Planning Committee of the Indian National Congress was set up in:
q.x: The NPC was formed in 1938 under Bose's presidency with Nehru as chairman.

q.s: The second round of bank nationalisation in India took place in:
q.x: Six banks were nationalised in April 1980; fourteen had been nationalised in 1969.

q.s: Under the UDAY scheme (2015), State governments took over what share of DISCOM debt?
q.x: States absorbed 75% of DISCOM debt in two years under UDAY.

q.s: The 'Indradhanush' plan of August 2015 related to:
q.x: Indradhanush was a seven-point plan for PSBs with ₹70,000 crore capital; Mission Indradhanush is the immunisation programme.

q.s: Between May 2022 and February 2023 the RBI raised the policy repo rate from 4.00% to:
q.x: The MPC raised the repo by 250 basis points to 6.50% to fight inflation.

q.s: IFCI, the first development finance institution of India, was set up in:
q.x: IFCI was set up in 1948; IDBI came in 1964 and NABARD in 1982.

q.s: The National Housing Bank was set up in 1988 as a wholly owned subsidiary of:
q.x: NHB was set up under the NHB Act, 1987, originally wholly owned by the RBI.

q.s: IDBI, set up in 1964 as a subsidiary of the RBI, was transferred to the Government of India in:
q.x: IDBI was delinked from the RBI in 1976; it became IDBI Ltd in 2004.

q.s: State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks are inspected by:
q.x: They are licensed by the RBI and inspected by NABARD.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT under the direct regulation of the RBI?
q.x: PACS are under the State Registrars of Cooperative Societies.

q.s: The Global Financial Crisis of 2007-09 originated in which market?
q.x: It surfaced in July 2007 in the US sub-prime housing loans that had been securitised worldwide.

q.s: Financing the fiscal deficit through external borrowing chiefly exposes the economy to:
q.x: External debt must be serviced in foreign currency, so a falling rupee raises the burden.

q.s: In Union Budget 2026-27, interest payments account for about how many paise of every rupee spent?
q.x: Interest takes about 20 paise of every rupee spent, about 40% of revenue receipts.

q.s: The Annual Financial Statement (the Budget) is laid before Parliament under which Article?
q.x: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement; Article 110 defines Money Bills.

q.s: According to the RBI's remittance survey (2023-24), the largest source of inward remittances to India is:
q.x: The USA accounted for 27.7%, followed by the UAE (19.2%) and the UK (10.8%).

q.s: In 2024, which country received the largest amount of remittances in the world?
q.x: India received about $129 billion, followed by Mexico.

q.s: Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre in which city of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Google's AI hub is planned at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the PDS in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Ragi and jowar are supplied at full market price.
Andhra Pradesh had 29,796 Fair Price Shops in 2024-25.
Doorstep delivery ended for all cardholders without exception.
Rice cards continue to serve as Aarogyasri eligibility cards.
q.x: Doorstep delivery stays for those aged 65+ and the disabled, millets are free and rice cards were delinked from Aarogyasri.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered under 'Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India' (BGREI)?
q.x: BGREI covers Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Eastern UP and West Bengal.

q.s: BGREI is a sub-scheme of which programme?
o: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
q.x: BGREI was launched in 2010-11 under the RKVY.

q.s: India's first agricultural university, set up in 1960, was located at:
q.x: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, was the first; PAU Ludhiana came in 1962.

q.s: The high-yielding wheat seeds imported in 1966 at the start of the Green Revolution came from:
q.x: About 18,000 tonnes of Mexican dwarf wheat seed were imported; rice HYVs came from the IRRI, Philippines.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of low farm productivity in India?
q.x: The lack, not abundance, of cold chains causes losses; only about 26% of pulse area is irrigated.

q.s: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) gives priority to which of the following?
o: Biological control such as neem-based pesticides
q.x: IPM combines biological and cultural methods with need-based chemical use.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land reforms in India is correct?
o: Land ceiling facilitates redistribution of surplus land.
Land ceiling fixes the maximum rent payable by tenants.
Land reforms tend to increase rural inequality.
Tenancy reform fixes the maximum land a family may own.
q.x: Ceilings cap holdings so surplus land can be redistributed; rent is fixed by tenancy reform.

q.s: The One Nation One Ration Card scheme is run by the:
o: Department of Food and Public Distribution
q.x: ONORC, enabling ration portability through ePoS and Aadhaar, is run by the Department of Food and Public Distribution.

q.s: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 by which Ministry?
q.x: MeitY runs Digital India, whose first pillar is Broadband Highways.

q.s: The BharatNet project aims to provide optical fibre connectivity up to the level of:
q.x: BharatNet (formerly NOFN) takes fibre to about 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats.

q.s: In 2023-24, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest per capita GDDP?
q.x: Visakhapatnam led with ₹5,45,588 per capita GDDP and also the highest GDDP.

q.s: The headquarters of which naval command is located at Visakhapatnam?
q.x: Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command; the Southern Command is at Kochi.

q.s: Sri City in Tirupati district is a:
q.x: Sri City on the AP-Tamil Nadu border is a multi-product SEZ.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, pension liabilities were divided between AP and Telangana on the basis of:
q.x: Pensions were divided by the population ratio of 58.32 : 41.68.

q.s: Which of the following is a Central Sector scheme, fully funded by the Centre?
q.x: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme; NHM and ICDS are Centrally Sponsored Schemes.

q.s: The usual funding ratio between the Centre and the States for Centrally Sponsored Schemes is:
q.x: CSS are shared 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, assets were generally divided on the basis of:
q.x: Assets went by location and liabilities by population ratio.

q.s: Which body directed Andhra Pradesh to pay Telangana its share of a central subsidy credited to AP?
q.x: The Southern Zonal Council handles such inter-State bifurcation issues.

q.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh receives the lowest annual rainfall?
q.x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone (Rayalaseema) gets 500-750 mm; the High Altitude and Tribal zone gets above 1,400 mm.

q.s: The greenfield Ramayapatnam port is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Ramayapatnam, 93 km north of Krishnapatnam, is now in Prakasam district.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor, India's first coastal corridor, is funded by the:
q.x: The ADB funds the VCIC, Phase 1 of the East Coast Economic Corridor.

q.s: Orvakal in Kurnool district is a node of which industrial corridor?
q.x: Orvakal is a node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor.

q.s: The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) functions under the:
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
q.x: NICDC, formerly DMICDC, works under DPIIT of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

q.s: The SVAMITVA scheme, which issues Property Cards to rural households using drone surveys, is implemented by the:
q.x: SVAMITVA is run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with the Survey of India as technology partner.

q.s: Petrol prices in India were decontrolled on 26 June 2010. Diesel prices were decontrolled in:
q.x: Diesel was decontrolled on 19 October 2014.

q.s: The Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) of 2016 replaced NELP's production-sharing with:
q.x: HELP moved to a revenue-sharing model with a uniform licence for all hydrocarbons.

q.s: The Fundamental Duty to protect and improve the natural environment is contained in:
q.x: Article 51A(g) is the citizen's duty; Article 48A is the Directive Principle for the State.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment.
Article 21 has been held not to include a clean environment.
q.x: 48A is a DPSP, 51A(g) a Fundamental Duty, and Article 21 has been read to include a clean environment.

q.s: Which is the hottest planet of the solar system?
q.x: Venus is hottest because of its dense carbon dioxide atmosphere, though Mercury is nearer the Sun.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the planets is correct?
o: Mercury has the shortest day of all planets.
Saturn rotates fastest of all planets.
Earth is the densest planet of the solar system.
q.x: Earth is densest; Jupiter has the shortest day (about 10 hours) and Venus is the hottest.

q.s: The average duration of the sunspot (solar) cycle is about:
q.x: Sunspot maxima recur about every 11 years.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Sun is correct?
o: Solar flares are caused by nuclear fission.
X-class solar flares are the strongest flares.
The solar cycle has no fixed periodicity.
Sunspots are hotter and brighter than the photosphere.
q.x: Flares come from magnetic reconnection, X-class being strongest; sunspots are cooler and darker.

q.s: The total geographical area of India is about:
q.x: India's area is 32,87,263 sq km, extending from 8°4'N to 37°6'N.

q.s: The east-west extent of the Indian mainland is about:
q.x: India is about 2,933 km east-west and 3,214 km north-south.

q.s: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
q.x: Norway, lying partly beyond the Arctic Circle, sees the midnight sun near the summer solstice.

q.s: Christmas falls in the summer season in which of the following countries?
q.x: In the Southern Hemisphere, December-January is summer as the South Pole tilts towards the Sun.

q.s: Standing waves set up in lakes and reservoirs by earthquakes are called:
q.x: Seiches are oscillating standing waves in enclosed water bodies.

q.s: The transformation of water-saturated soft soil into a fluid-like mass during an earthquake is known as:
q.x: Liquefaction affects saturated soft soils such as those of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

q.s: The Nilgiris are an example of which type of mountain?
q.x: The Nilgiris, Aravallis and Vindhyas are residual mountains; the Salt Range is a block mountain.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a residual mountain?
q.x: Kilimanjaro is a volcanic mountain.

q.s: India's first geothermal wells were drilled by ONGC at Puga Valley in:
q.x: ONGC drilled India's first geothermal wells at Puga in Ladakh.

q.s: The famous geyser 'Old Faithful' is located in:
q.x: Old Faithful is in Yellowstone National Park, which has the most geysers.

q.s: Popocatepetl volcano is located in which country?
q.x: Popocatepetl is in Mexico; Volcan de Fuego is in Guatemala.

q.s: Which of the following volcanoes is NOT located in the Americas?
q.x: Whakaari is in New Zealand; Tungurahua is in Ecuador.

q.s: A lake formed when a meander loop is cut off from the main river is called a(n):
q.x: Oxbow lakes form when a river cuts through the neck of a meander.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a depositional landform of a river?
q.x: A gorge is carved by vertical erosion; levees, deltas and flood plains are built by deposition.

q.s: Why are plateaus often called tablelands?
o: They have a broad flat top and steep sides
They are formed only by rivers
q.x: A plateau's elevated flat top rising sharply above surroundings looks like a table.

q.s: Dust and salt particles on which water vapour condenses in the atmosphere are called:
q.x: Condensation takes place on hygroscopic nuclei such as dust, smoke and salt.

q.s: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is generally associated with more cyclones in the:
q.x: Positive IOD favours Arabian Sea cyclones; negative IOD favours Bay of Bengal cyclones.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is correct?
o: It is a sea-temperature pattern of the Pacific Ocean.
A positive IOD brings more Bay of Bengal cyclones.
A negative IOD increases Indian monsoon rainfall.
It runs independently of ENSO but interacts with it.
q.x: The IOD is an Indian Ocean pattern distinct from ENSO; a negative IOD reduces Indian rainfall.

q.s: The Gulf Stream begins in the Gulf of Mexico as the:
q.x: The Gulf Stream starts as the Florida Current and continues as the North Atlantic Drift.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a warm ocean current?
q.x: The Humboldt (Peru) current is cold; warm currents usually flow along east coasts in low and middle latitudes.

q.s: The Atacama desert owes its extreme dryness partly to which cold ocean current?
q.x: The Humboldt current off Chile and Peru keeps the Atacama dry; the Benguela affects the Namib.

q.s: Which warm current keeps the ports of Norway and Murmansk ice-free in winter?
q.x: The North Atlantic Drift warms north-west Europe.

q.s: Which State of India receives the maximum rainfall from the north-east monsoon?
q.x: The Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain in October-December.

q.s: In 2015-16, the Integrated Watershed Management Programme was merged into which scheme?
q.x: IWMP became the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a method of improving soil fertility?
q.x: Fertility is improved by rotation and manuring; seed modification does not enrich the soil.

q.s: The Koyna earthquake of 1967 in Maharashtra is a well-known example of a(n):
q.x: Koyna is attributed to the Shivajisagar reservoir; Killari (1993) was an intraplate quake.

q.s: Which earthquake led to the enactment of the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
q.x: The Bhuj quake of 26 January 2001 led to the DM Act and NDMA.

q.s: Under the disaster management framework, who is regarded as the first responder in a disaster?
q.x: The community is always first on the spot; the district administration has the basic responsibility.

q.s: India became the first 'Pioneer Investor' for deep-sea mining in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in:
q.x: India got Pioneer Investor status in 1987 for polymetallic nodules.

q.s: About 98 per cent of India's coal reserves are found in which rock system?
q.x: Gondwana rocks hold most coal; Tertiary rocks have petroleum and Neyveli lignite.

q.s: Which of the following coal deposits is NOT of Gondwana age?
q.x: Neyveli lignite is Tertiary; Jharia, Raniganj and Singareni are Gondwana coalfields.

q.s: Which of the following is a field-based (near the oilfield) refinery?
q.x: Digboi in Assam is a field-based refinery; Mathura is market-based.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam oil refinery is operated by:
q.x: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation operates the Visakhapatnam refinery.

q.s: The Bhadla Solar Park, among the largest in the world, is located in:
q.x: Bhadla is in Jodhpur district of Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of renewable energy park and State is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Pavagada (2,050 MW) is in Karnataka.

q.s: The headquarters of the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) is at:
q.x: MPEDA, a statutory body under the Commerce Ministry, is based at Kochi.

q.s: How many agro-climatic zones are there in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: AP has six agro-climatic zones.

q.s: The Annadatha Sukhibhava scheme of Andhra Pradesh is a State top-up to which Central scheme?
q.x: Annadatha Sukhibhava adds State support to PM-KISAN.

q.s: In horticulture production (2021-22), Andhra Pradesh does NOT rank first in which crop?
q.x: AP is second in mango (Uttar Pradesh is first) but first in oil palm, papaya and tomato.

q.s: Which State has the highest road density in India?
q.x: Kerala has the highest road density.

q.s: National Highways form about 2 per cent of India's road length but carry about what share of road traffic?
q.x: NHs carry about 40% of road traffic.

q.s: The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets a port handling capacity of:
q.x: The Vision targets 10 billion tonnes per annum by 2047.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Sagarmala programme?
q.x: Sagarmala's pillars are port modernisation, connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development and coastal shipping.

q.s: Which of the following ports of Andhra Pradesh is NOT developed under a PPP model?
q.x: Kakinada Anchorage is State-run by the AP Maritime Board; Gangavaram is BOOT and Krishnapatnam BOST.

q.s: Mulapeta port in Srikakulam district was earlier known as:
q.x: The Bhavanapadu port project was renamed Mulapeta.

q.s: Dugarajapatnam, promised as a major port in the 13th Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, now lies in which district?
q.x: Dugarajapatnam is now in Tirupati district.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh is India's largest producer of which export variety of tobacco?
q.x: AP leads in FCV tobacco, the main export variety, and ranks first in tobacco exports.

q.s: As per Census 2011 data on the present 28-district map, the least literate district of Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju has the lowest literacy (44.67%); Visakhapatnam the highest (79.05%).

q.s: On the earlier 13-district map (Census 2011), the most literate district of Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: West Godavari (74.6%) was most literate and Vizianagaram (58.9%) least.

q.s: In the Human Development Index, 'mean years of schooling' is measured for adults aged:
q.x: Mean years of schooling covers adults 25+; expected years of schooling is for children of school-entry age.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the Human Development Index?
q.x: Gender inequality is measured separately by the GII; HDI uses health, education and GNI per capita.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of a country's human capital?
q.x: Trust and harmony form social capital; literacy, skills and health form human capital.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the largest Scheduled Caste population?
q.x: Prakasam had both the highest share and largest number of SCs.

q.s: In India, the child sex ratio refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group:
q.x: CSR is girls per 1,000 boys aged 0-6; India expresses the overall sex ratio as females per 1,000 males.

q.s: The e-Shram portal, launched on 26 August 2021, is a national database of:
q.x: e-Shram registers unorganised workers and gives each a 12-digit Universal Account Number.

q.s: Between Census 2001 and Census 2011, the child sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh:
q.x: The child sex ratio fell from 961 to 939, though the overall sex ratio improved.

q.s: The Koya and Kondh tribes oppose the Polavaram project mainly because it will:
q.x: Polavaram's reservoir will submerge about 276 villages, largely tribal.

q.s: The Shompen tribe of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands lives on:
q.x: The Shompen live on Great Nicobar; the Onge on Little Andaman and the Sentinelese on North Sentinel.

q.s: Which of the following tribes is NOT found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
q.x: The Toda live in the Nilgiri hills of Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following tribes does NOT belong to the Southern tribal zone of India?
q.x: The Bhil belong to the Western zone; Chenchu, Koya and Toda are southern tribes.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a primary activity?
q.x: Call-centre work is a tertiary service; dairy, bee-keeping and fishing are primary.

q.s: Which is the most common type of coral reef found in India?
q.x: Fringing reefs are commonest in India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about coral reefs is correct?
o: A barrier reef is separated from the coast by a wide, deep lagoon.
Barrier reefs are the commonest type in India.
An atoll encloses a lagoon with central land.
Fringing reefs lie far out in the open ocean.
q.x: An atoll's lagoon has no central land; fringing reefs grow close to the shore.

q.s: The neritic zone of the ocean, the richest fishing zone, lies over the:
q.x: The neritic zone extends over the shelf to about 200 m.

q.s: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a UNESCO natural World Heritage Site in:
q.x: The Western Ghats were listed in 2012; Great Himalayan National Park in 2014.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT traversed by the Western Ghats?
q.x: The Western Ghats run through Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: India's first two Ramsar sites, designated in 1981, were Chilika Lake and:
q.x: Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo (Rajasthan) were designated in 1981.

q.s: Which is the largest Ramsar site in India?
q.x: The Sunderbans wetland in West Bengal is India's largest Ramsar site.

q.s: If the crude birth rate is 30 per 1,000 and the crude death rate 10 per 1,000, the annual rate of natural increase is:
In disaster management, risk is generally expressed as:
q.x: Risk rises with hazard and vulnerability and falls with capacity.

q.s: Abhijit Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economics with Esther Duflo and:
q.x: The 2019 prize went to Banerjee, Duflo and Kremer for experimental approaches to poverty.

q.s: V. Ramakrishnan won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work on the:
q.x: Ramakrishnan studied the structure and function of the ribosome.

q.s: Which country ranks second in the world in gross expenditure on R&D as a share of GDP, at about 5%?
q.x: South Korea spends about 5% of GDP on R&D, behind Israel.

q.s: After the abolition of the Intellectual Property Appellate Board in 2021, patent appeals are heard by the:
q.x: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 shifted IPAB's work to the High Courts.

q.s: The National Atmospheric Research Laboratory (NARL) is located at:
q.x: NARL is at Gadanki near Tirupati; SDSC-SHAR is at Sriharikota.

q.s: Which of the following space or defence facilities is NOT located in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: VSSC is at Thiruvananthapuram; SDSC-SHAR, NSTL Visakhapatnam and NARL Gadanki are in AP.

q.s: Under the National Quantum Mission, the thematic hub for Quantum Computing is hosted by:
q.x: IISc hosts Quantum Computing; IIT Madras hosts Quantum Communication.

q.s: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is a market mechanism under which national mission?
o: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency
q.x: PAT under NMEEE issues tradable Energy Saving Certificates to units beating targets.

q.s: Under the PAT scheme, units that exceed their energy-saving targets earn:
q.x: Surplus savings are certified as ESCerts, traded on power exchanges.

q.s: The reusable rocket 'New Glenn' is developed by:
q.x: New Glenn is Blue Origin's; Starship is SpaceX's.

q.s: Which of the following reusable rockets is NOT developed by an American company?
q.x: Zhuque-3 is built by China's LandSpace.

q.s: Oceansat-3, launched in 2022 on PSLV-C54, was renamed:
q.x: Oceansat-3 is EOS-06; Oceansat-1 was launched in 1999.

q.s: Which of the following CANNOT be done using satellite remote sensing at present?
o: Monitoring ground deformation after a quake
q.x: Earthquakes cannot be predicted; post-event deformation and inundation can be mapped.

q.s: The lunar module of Apollo 11 that landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969 was named:
q.x: Eagle was the lunar module; Columbia was the command module.

q.s: Japan's SLIM mission made Japan which country to soft-land on the Moon?
q.x: After the USSR, USA, China and India, Japan became the fifth.

q.s: 'Varunastra', developed by NSTL Visakhapatnam, is a:
q.x: Varunastra is a ship-launched heavyweight torpedo; Maareech is a decoy and USHUS a sonar.

q.s: The Swathi radar made by BEL is a:
q.x: Swathi locates enemy guns, mortars and rockets; it has been exported to Armenia.

q.s: Under the IGMDP, which missile is a liquid-fuelled surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile?
q.x: Prithvi has a range of 150-350 km; Akash is a surface-to-air missile.

q.s: Which IGMDP missile was shut down in 2008 without induction into the Army?
q.x: The Trishul programme was closed in 2008.

q.s: The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme was launched in 1983 under the leadership of:
q.x: Kalam led IGMDP with DRDL Hyderabad as lead laboratory.

q.s: Which of the following missiles was NOT developed under the IGMDP?
q.x: BrahMos is an Indo-Russian joint venture; IGMDP covered Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul and Nag.

q.s: In 2025, the Disha SOS app of Andhra Pradesh was replaced by the:
q.x: Disha SOS (2020) was replaced by the Suraksha app in 2025.

q.s: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) functions under the:
q.x: I4C is under MHA; NCIIPC is under NTRO.

q.s: Which body protects India's critical information infrastructure?
q.x: NCIIPC, under NTRO, protects critical information infrastructure; CERT-In handles general cyber incidents.

q.s: Which month is observed as cyber security awareness month in India?
q.x: October is cyber security awareness month; Cyber Jagrookta Diwas is the first Wednesday of every month.

q.s: In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), which section of the IT Act was struck down?
q.x: Section 66A was struck down under Article 19(1)(a); 69A was upheld and 79 read down.

q.s: The 'Right to Be Forgotten' under the EU's GDPR corresponds to the right to:
q.x: Article 17 of the GDPR provides the right to erasure, the 'right to be forgotten'.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an explicit statutory right under India's DPDP Act, 2023?
q.x: Data portability is a GDPR right (Article 20) but not given in the DPDP Act.

q.s: Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators used on spacecraft like Voyager are fuelled by:
q.x: RTGs use Pu-238 decay heat.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG) is correct?
o: It drives a steam turbine with decay heat.
It converts decay heat into electricity using thermocouples.
It works only on the Earth's surface.
q.x: An RTG has no moving parts; thermocouples convert heat into electricity.

q.s: Flue-gas desulphurisation (FGD) units are installed in coal power plants to reduce emission of:
q.x: FGD scrubbers trap SO2 from flue gas.

q.s: The nodal agency for the Saubhagya scheme of household electrification is:
q.x: REC is the nodal agency for both DDUGJY and Saubhagya.

q.s: Which of the following statements about rural electrification is correct?
o: DDUGJY was launched in December 2014 with REC as the nodal agency.
PFC is the nodal agency of the Saubhagya scheme.
Farm feeders under RDSS are solarised under PM-KISAN.
q.x: DDUGJY (3 December 2014) had REC as nodal agency; separated farm feeders are solarised under PM-KUSUM.

q.s: The biggest driver of India's trade deficit is the import of:
q.x: Crude oil imports dominate the import bill, so oil price rises widen the deficit.

q.s: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency is a statutory body under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
q.x: BEE, set up under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, works under the Ministry of Power.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 is correct?
o: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency works under MNRE.
It applies only to household appliances.
Designated consumers must carry out mandatory energy audits.
q.x: BEE began work on 1 March 2002; the Act covers designated consumers, appliances and buildings.

q.s: India's coal production crossed one billion tonnes for the first time in:
q.x: Output in 2024-25 was about 1,047.5 MT.

q.s: Which is the highest dam in India?
q.x: Tehri is higher than Bhakra; Idukki comes next.

q.s: The Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) mainly applies to:
q.x: DISCOMs and designated consumers must buy a share of renewable power.

q.s: The Pinnapuram Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project is located in which district?
q.x: Pinnapuram IRESP is in Kurnool district; Gandikota PSP is in YSR Kadapa.

q.s: The Dr Narla Tatarao Thermal Power Station (Dr NTTPS) is located at:
q.x: Dr NTTPS is at Ibrahimpatnam near Vijayawada; RTPP is at Muddanur.

q.s: The main invasive plant threatening the Banni grassland of Kutch is:
q.x: Prosopis juliflora (vilayati babul) has spread widely over Banni.

q.s: Frankia, a nitrogen-fixing actinomycete, forms root nodules with which plants?
q.x: Frankia fixes nitrogen with non-legumes such as Alnus and Casuarina.

q.s: Bacillus megaterium is used as a biofertiliser because it:
q.x: It is a phosphate-solubilising bacterium (PSB).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the IUCN Red List criteria A to E?
o: Value of the species in international trade
q.x: The criteria rest on decline, range, small population and extinction-risk analysis, not trade value.

q.s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the tiger?
q.x: The tiger is Endangered; the Siberian crane is Critically Endangered.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN?
q.x: The tiger is Endangered; the other three are Critically Endangered.

q.s: Water hyacinth, called the 'Terror of Bengal', is native to:
q.x: Water hyacinth comes from the Amazon basin of South America.

q.s: A 'carbon bomb' is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting over its lifetime more than:
q.x: Carbon bombs are projects able to emit over 1 Gt CO2; Gevra (Chhattisgarh) is one in India.

q.s: India became the first country to adopt a National Agroforestry Policy in:
q.x: India adopted the policy in February 2014.

q.s: The ICAR-Central Agroforestry Research Institute is located at:
